title: Bengaluru home-care brand cut subscription churn from 42% to 24% with a per-SKU WhatsApp refill engine
content: SITUATION: A Bengaluru D2C home-care brand (floor cleaner, dishwash, laundry refills) at ~₹6 Cr ARR sold on its own site plus Blinkit and Zepto. Monthly subscription churn was 42%, blended CAC ₹680, AOV ₹540 at 46% gross margin — so a subscriber needed ~3 cycles just to clear acquisition cost. The real insight: 61% of cancellations hit in months 2-3, because fixed day-30 auto-renew billed BEFORE the previous pack ran out, triggering an 'I still have stock, cancel' reflex. ACTION: We killed calendar billing and built a refill engine on the official WhatsApp Business API. Instead of charging on day 30, a 'Running low? Reorder in 1 tap' message fired on each SKU's real consumption cycle (laundry ~38 days, dishwash ~22 days) with UPI one-tap checkout. We also shifted trial acquisition off cold Meta prospecting to Blinkit/Zepto ₹49 starter packs, then converted those buyers to subscription on WhatsApp, not email. OUTCOME: Over 4 months churn fell to 24%, repeat-purchase rate rose 31%, the WhatsApp reorder flow hit 18% click-to-buy versus 2.3% on email, starter-pack-to-subscription conversion ran 9%, and LTV:CAC moved from 1.9x to 3.4x. Net subscriber base grew 27% on flat ₹8-12L/month spend.
lesson: Churn in Indian D2C consumables is usually a TIMING problem, not a loyalty problem. Bill on each customer's real per-SKU consumption cycle, never a fixed calendar date, so you never charge while their cupboard is still full. Replace email nudges with one-tap WhatsApp + UPI reorders, and acquire trials cheaply via ₹49 Blinkit/Zepto sampling before converting to subscription on WhatsApp — it beats cold Meta prospecting on both CAC and retention.
